claim: The World Health Organization has called for research into predictive factors for selecting persons who could be successfully treated with shorter durations of direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy for hepatitis C.
source: World Health Organization has called for research into predictive factors for selecting persons who could be successfully treated with shorter durations of direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy for hepatitis C.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to the World Health Organization (2018) in the manuscript text.

claim: In Vietnam, a standard 12-week course of sofosbuvir and daclatasvir (SOF/DCV) was priced at US$2417–2472 in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC) in 2019.
source: A standard 12-week course of sofosbuvir and daclatasvir (SOF/DCV) was priced at US$2417–2472 in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC) in 2019 (Nguyen Thanh et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nguyen Thanh et al., 2019.

claim: The Ministry of Health estimates only 1000 individuals accessed DAA treatment through health insurance in 2019, and 2700 in 2020 in Vietnam.
source: the Ministry of Health estimates only 1000 individuals accessed DAA treatment through health insurance in 2019, and 2700 in 2020 (Ministry of Health V, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ministry of Health V, 2021.

claim: Pooled sustained virological response (SVR) for HCV DAA regimens of ≤4 weeks duration was 63.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 39.9–83.7).
source: A systematic review and meta-analysis into treatment optimisation for HCV with DAA therapy in individuals with favourable predictors of response, found that pooled sustained virological response (SVR) for regimens of ≤4 weeks duration was 63.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 39.9–83.7), 6 weeks duration was 81.1% (75.1–86.6) and 8 weeks duration was 94.2% (92.3–95.9) (Jones et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jones et al., 2019, which is a systematic review and meta-analysis.

claim: Pooled sustained virological response (SVR) for HCV DAA regimens of 6 weeks duration was 81.1% (75.1–86.6).
source: A systematic review and meta-analysis into treatment optimisation for HCV with DAA therapy in individuals with favourable predictors of response, found that pooled sustained virological response (SVR) for regimens of ≤4 weeks duration was 63.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 39.9–83.7), 6 weeks duration was 81.1% (75.1–86.6) and 8 weeks duration was 94.2% (92.3–95.9) (Jones et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jones et al., 2019, which is a systematic review and meta-analysis.

claim: Pooled sustained virological response (SVR) for HCV DAA regimens of 8 weeks duration was 94.2% (92.3–95.9).
source: A systematic review and meta-analysis into treatment optimisation for HCV with DAA therapy in individuals with favourable predictors of response, found that pooled sustained virological response (SVR) for regimens of ≤4 weeks duration was 63.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 39.9–83.7), 6 weeks duration was 81.1% (75.1–86.6) and 8 weeks duration was 94.2% (92.3–95.9) (Jones et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jones et al., 2019, which is a systematic review and meta-analysis.

claim: Response-guided therapy (RGT) was routinely used in the era of interferon-based therapy, when an undetectable HCV RNA at 4 weeks was used to determine a shorter course of pegylated interferon and ribavirin.
source: So-called response-guided therapy (RGT), whereby antiviral duration is shortened in individuals who rapidly suppress virus levels in blood after starting treatment, was routinely used in the era of interferon-based therapy, when an undetectable HCV RNA at 4 weeks was used to determine a shorter course of pegylated interferon and ribavirin (Fried et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fried et al., 2011.

claim: High cure rates were observed with just 3 weeks triple therapy (protease inhibitor [PI], NS5A inhibitor and NS5B inhibitor) in genotype 1b infection when day 2 viral load was used to determine treatment duration.
source: In this population, high cure rates were observed with just 3 weeks triple therapy (protease inhibitor [PI], NS5A inhibitor and NS5B inhibitor) (Lau et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lau et al., 2016.

claim: All 10 individuals who became undetectable at D3 of treatment achieved first-line SVR12 regardless of treatment duration in a UK treatment shortening study using 4–8 weeks ombitasvir, paritaprevir, dasabuvir and ritonavir.
source: In a UK treatment shortening study, which used 4–8 weeks ombitasvir, paritaprevir, dasabuvir and ritonavir based on baseline viral load, all 10 individuals who became undetectable at D3 of treatment achieved first-line SVR12 regardless of treatment duration(Cooke and Pett, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cooke and Pett, 2021.

claim: There is currently no data for RGT durations less than 8 weeks with SOF/DCV.
source: There is currently no data for RGT durations less than 8 weeks with SOF/DCV, which remains the lowest-priced and most widely available treatment option globally (Clinton Health Access Initiative, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Clinton Health Access Initiative, 2021, and represents a statement about the absence of data at the time of writing.

claim: SOF/DCV remains the lowest-priced and most widely available treatment option globally for hepatitis C.
source: There is currently no data for RGT durations less than 8 weeks with SOF/DCV, which remains the lowest-priced and most widely available treatment option globally (Clinton Health Access Initiative, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Clinton Health Access Initiative, 2021.

claim: Vietnam has a high burden of genotype 6 HCV infection (around 35%).
source: Vietnam has a high burden of genotype 6 HCV infection (around 35%) (Irekeola et al., 2021), which is rare outside South East Asia and under-represented in clinical trials.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Irekeola et al., 2021.

claim: Genotype 6 HCV is rare outside South East Asia and under-represented in clinical trials.
source: Vietnam has a high burden of genotype 6 HCV infection (around 35%) (Irekeola et al., 2021), which is rare outside South East Asia and under-represented in clinical trials.

claim: Genotype 6 is the most genetically diverse HCV lineage.
source: Genotype 6 is the most genetically diverse HCV lineage (Hedskog et al., 2019), raising concerns about the potential for emergence of resistant variants (McPhee et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hedskog et al., 2019.

claim: The human IFNL4 di-nucleotide polymorphism rs368234815 (ΔG/TT) controls generation of the IFNL4 protein.
source: The human IFNL4 di-nucleotide polymorphism rs368234815 (ΔG/TT) controls generation of the IFNL4 protein and is also associated with impaired clearance of HCV Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013 and inferior responses to pegylated interferon-alpha/ribavirin therapy (Franco et al., 2014) and SOF-based treatment (Ansari et al., 2017; Ansari et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013.

claim: The human IFNL4 di-nucleotide polymorphism rs368234815 (ΔG/TT) is associated with impaired clearance of HCV.
source: The human IFNL4 di-nucleotide polymorphism rs368234815 (ΔG/TT) controls generation of the IFNL4 protein and is also associated with impaired clearance of HCV Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013 and inferior responses to pegylated interferon-alpha/ribavirin therapy (Franco et al., 2014) and SOF-based treatment (Ansari et al., 2017; Ansari et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013.

claim: The human IFNL4 di-nucleotide polymorphism rs368234815 (ΔG/TT) is associated with inferior responses to pegylated interferon-alpha/ribavirin therapy.
source: The human IFNL4 di-nucleotide polymorphism rs368234815 (ΔG/TT) controls generation of the IFNL4 protein and is also associated with impaired clearance of HCV Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013 and inferior responses to pegylated interferon-alpha/ribavirin therapy (Franco et al., 2014) and SOF-based treatment (Ansari et al., 2017; Ansari et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Franco et al., 2014.

claim: The human IFNL4 di-nucleotide polymorphism rs368234815 (ΔG/TT) is associated with inferior responses to SOF-based treatment.
source: The human IFNL4 di-nucleotide polymorphism rs368234815 (ΔG/TT) controls generation of the IFNL4 protein and is also associated with impaired clearance of HCV Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013 and inferior responses to pegylated interferon-alpha/ribavirin therapy (Franco et al., 2014) and SOF-based treatment (Ansari et al., 2017; Ansari et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ansari et al., 2017 and Ansari et al., 2019.

claim: Participants were recruited from the outpatient hepatitis clinic of the Hospital for Tropical Diseases (HTD) in HCMC, between February 2019 and June 2020.
source: Participants were recruited from the outpatient hepatitis clinic of the Hospital for Tropical Diseases (HTD) in HCMC, between February 2019 and June 2020.
evidence: The claim describes the study population and recruitment period as stated in the methods.

claim: Eligible patients were ≥18 years and had chronic infection with HCV genotype 1 or 6 without evidence of liver fibrosis (defined as a FibroScan score≤7.1 kPa, equivalent to F0-F1 disease).
source: Eligible patients were ≥18 years and had chronic infection with HCV genotype 1 or 6 without evidence of liver fibrosis (defined as a FibroScan score≤7.1 kPa, equivalent to F0-F1 disease) (Nitta et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim describes the eligibility criteria for the study, with a citation to Nitta et al., 2009 for the FibroScan threshold definition.

claim: All participants were treated with sofosbuvir 400 mg and daclatasvir 60 mg (Pharco Pharmaceuticals, Egypt) administered orally as two separate tablets, once daily.
source: All participants were treated with sofosbuvir 400 mg and daclatasvir 60 mg (Pharco Pharmaceuticals, Egypt) administered orally as two separate tablets, once daily.
evidence: The claim describes the treatment regimen used in the study.

claim: Treatment duration was determined using hepatitis C viral load measured 2 days after treatment onset (D2).
source: Treatment duration was determined using hepatitis C viral load measured 2 days after treatment onset (D2).
evidence: The claim describes the study design for determining treatment duration.

claim: Participants with viral load <500 IU/ml at D2 (after two doses of SOF/DCV) were treated with 4-week SOF/DCV.
source: Participants with viral load <500 IU/ml at D2 (after two doses of SOF/DCV) were treated with 4-week SOF/DCV.
evidence: The claim describes the study protocol for treatment allocation.

claim: Those with HCV RNA≥500 IU/ml at D2 received 8 weeks of SOF/DCV.
source: Those with HCV RNA≥500 IU/ml received 8 weeks (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim describes the study protocol for treatment allocation, with reference to Figure 1.

claim: The study by Lau et al., 2016 reported 100% SVR12 following 3-week triple therapy using a threshold of 500 IU/ml at day 2.
source: The aforementioned study by Lau et al., 2016 reported 100% SVR12 following 3-week triple therapy using this threshold.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lau et al., 2016.

claim: The primary endpoint was sustained virological response (SVR12) defined as plasma HCV RNA less than the lower limit of quantification (<LLOQ) 12 weeks after the EOT without prior failure.
source: The primary endpoint was sustained virological response (SVR12) defined as plasma HCV RNA less than the lower limit of quantification (<LLOQ) 12 weeks after the EOT without prior failure.
evidence: The claim describes the primary endpoint definition for the study.

claim: Failure of first-line treatment required two consecutive viral loads >LLOQ, taken at least 1 week apart, with the second >2000 IU/ml.
source: Failure of first-line treatment was carefully defined to incorporate individuals who fully suppressed HCV RNA (<LLOQ) on therapy with late virological rebound, as well as those who never fully suppressed HCV viral load. In both cases, two consecutive viral loads >LLOQ, taken at least 1 week apart, were required to confirm failure, with the second >2000 IU/ml.
evidence: The claim describes the study protocol for defining treatment failure.

claim: Once failure was confirmed, participants commenced retreatment with standard duration SOF/DCV within 2 weeks.
source: Once failure was confirmed, participants commenced retreatment with standard duration SOF/DCV within 2 weeks (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim describes the study protocol for retreatment, with reference to Figure 1.

claim: Assuming 90% power and one-sided α=0.05, 37 participants were required to exclude the null hypothesis that cure was <90%.
source: Assuming 90% power and one-sided α=0.05, 37 participants were required to exclude the null hypothesis that cure was <90%.
evidence: The claim describes the sample size calculation for the study.

claim: Assuming 5% loss to follow-up, and that 65% would suppress viral load <500 IU/ml by day 2 and receive 4 weeks (rather than 8 weeks) of therapy, the final target population was 60 participants.
source: Assuming 5% loss to follow-up, and that, based on the study by Lau et al., 2016, 65% would suppress viral load <500 IU/ml by day 2 and receive 4 weeks (rather than 8 weeks) of therapy, the final target population was 60 participants, pooling genotypes 1 and 6.
evidence: The claim describes the sample size calculation for the study, with a citation to Lau et al., 2016 for the assumption about the proportion suppressing viral load.

claim: HCV RNA was measured using the Abbott Architect (LLOQ=12 IU/ml) for the first 41 participants enrolled.
source: At start of study (for the first 41 participants enrolled), this was the Abbott Architect (LLOQ=12 IU/ml).
evidence: The claim describes the laboratory methods used in the study.

claim: HCV RNA was subsequently measured using the COBAS AmpliPrep/COBAS TaqMan HCV Quantitative Test, version 2.0 (Roche Molecular Systems, LLOQ=15 IU/ml).
source: This was subsequently replaced with the COBAS AmpliPrep/COBAS TaqMan HCV Quantitative Test, version 2.0 (Roche Molecular Systems, LLOQ=15 IU/ml).
evidence: The claim describes the laboratory methods used in the study.

claim: HCV genotype and subtype were determined using NS5B, Core and 5′ UTR sequencing, according to the method described by Le Ngoc et al., 2019.
source: At screening, HCV genotype and subtype were determined using NS5B, Core and 5′ UTR sequencing, according to the method described by Le Ngoc et al., 2019.
evidence: The claim describes the laboratory methods used in the study, with a citation to Le Ngoc et al., 2019.

claim: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on all enrolled participants' virus at baseline, and upon virological rebound and at start of retreatment in participants failing therapy.

claim: WGS of the HCV viral genome was attained using Illumina MiSeq platform as described previously.
source: WGS of the HCV viral genome was attained using Illumina MiSeq platform as described previously (Thomson et al., 2016; Smith et al., 2021b; Smith et al., 2021a; Manso et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim describes the laboratory methods used in the study, with citations to previous publications.

claim: RAS were only considered if present in at least 15% of the reads in the sample and had a read count of greater than 10.
source: We only looked for RAS that were present in at least 15% of the reads in the sample and had a read count of greater than 10.
evidence: The claim describes the analysis methods used in the study.

claim: The Public Health England (PHE) HCV Resistance Group's definition for RASs was used.

claim: Genotyping of IFNL4 rs368234815 was performed on host DNA using the TaqMan SNP genotyping assay and primers described previously.

evidence: The claim describes the laboratory methods used in the study, with a citation to Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013.

claim: The plasma drug levels of SOF, its inactive metabolite GS-331007, and DCV were measured at baseline, at day 14 and at EOT (day 28 or 56) in all participants.

evidence: The claim describes the study methods for pharmacokinetic assessment.

claim: Intensive drug level sampling was conducted in a subset of 40 participants.
source: In addition, intensive drug level sampling was conducted in a subset of 40 participants, who were sequentially invited to join an ancillary PK study.
evidence: The claim describes the study methods for pharmacokinetic assessment.

claim: Drug quantification was performed using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometer at Mahidol Oxford Tropical Medicine Research Unit, Bangkok.
source: Drug quantification was performed using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometer at Mahidol Oxford Tropical Medicine Research Unit, Bangkok.
evidence: The claim describes the laboratory methods used in the study.

claim: Of 455 patients screened, 52 were enrolled and 1 subsequently withdrew.
source: Of 455 patients screened, 52 were enrolled and 1 subsequently withdrew (Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in the results section and Figure 2.

source: Eighteen participants were above the threshold at this time point, of which 1 withdrew after 9 days of treatment, meaning 17 completed 8-week therapy.

evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in the results section, Figure 3, and Table 2.

source: The mean first-line SOF/DCV treatment duration was 37 days (standard deviation, SD 13.7), with a first-line cure rate of 75%.

source: The mean (SD) total SOF/DCV duration (i.e., including 12-week retreatment where required), was 58 (34.2) days per patient, with a 100% cure rate.

source: There was no evidence of differences in age, gender, BMI, IFNL4 genotype, transaminases or baseline HCV viral load between patients who achieved cure with 4-week treatment versus those who experienced treatment failure with 4-week treatment (Table 3).

claim: Day 7 HCV RNA<LLOQ had 90% sensitivity (95% CI [56, 100]) for predicting cure with 4-week treatment.

claim: The two HCV assays used in the study have previously been shown to yield different HCV RNA results in the same individuals on therapy.
